title: Leonard Bosdorfer and other young players who died early
summary: Leclerc recalls Leonard Bosdorfer, a fine young ear-player who died very young, and others (Guy McCormick, Eddie McCarty) who also died young.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But, uh... Do you remember Jimmy Boisot, H.J. Boisot? He used to own a printing company. He played wonderful ragtime piano.
Well, you know, you never mentioned, don't know who I never mentioned, a fellow by the name of Bosdorfer. He was very young. Leonard? Leonard Bosdorfer.
I knew Johnny, but I never knew Leonard.

Oh, Leonard. Leonard played. Oh, he died very young. Oh, I doubt whether he was in his twenties when he died. Well, that was before my time. He played by air too. And he was a very good piano player too. Leonard Bosdorfer, yeah. Yeah, I liked Leonard in those days. He was a wonderful fellow, but he died very, very young. Guy McCormick died. He was only 37 years old. When he died, he died of a heart attack. And my other father, Fuzzy Wuzzy Twins, he died rather young too. Now, Eddie?
McCaw? No, no. Guy McCormick. And Eddie? Eddie McCawty.
Eddie McCawty. Yeah, Eddie McCawty. Yeah, Eddie McCawty died quite young too.
What did Leonard Bosdorfer feature? Did he have any special numbers that he played of his own? No, no.
He played in one of the cafes.

around there, and he was young in those days as I say, much younger than I was, and he played very nice piano. He played, I forget the places where he played, but he was rather young and a very good piano player.
